en: Guard cells swell with water to open stomata, allowing carbon dioxide to enter the leaf for photosynthesis.
Hydrochloric acid in the stomach breaks down proteins and kills harmful bacteria swallowed with food.
A chameleon changes skin color by relaxing or contracting specialized pigment cells called chromatophores to blend into its surroundings.
Fungi secrete enzymes that break down dead mango leaves, returning essential nutrients to the soil for new plants.
Thin capillary walls allow oxygen and nutrients from the blood to pass directly into surrounding body cells.
The fibrous husk of a coconut traps air, enabling the seed to float across the ocean to sprout elsewhere.
Sensory nerves send a signal to the spinal cord, which instantly triggers motor nerves to pull a hand away from heat.
Tadpoles secrete enzymes that dissolve their tails, absorbing the nutrients to fuel the growth of their adult frog legs.
White blood cells produce specific antibodies that lock onto invading dengue viruses to neutralize them and prevent further infection.
Water evaporating from leaves creates a pulling force that draws more water up through the xylem from the roots.
Water flowing over a fish gill pushes oxygen through thin filaments directly into its bloodstream while releasing carbon dioxide.
A camel hump stores fat, which the body metabolizes into energy and water when food is scarce in the desert.
